task.name: Seam-test coverage batch: adaptive routing and model registry (5 findings)
task.story_text:
## What

Verified missing-seam-coverage findings from TheForge's own review pool. This
batch adds the missing tests as one sweep.

Each item names the seam by the behaviour it guards and states what is not
exercised. Nothing is located by line: this batch has already had one item go
obsolete and another drift by more than a hundred lines while sitting in the
backlog, which is what citing coordinates buys.

## Why

Consolidated from 6 individual forge-finding issues during the restart findings
sweep on 2026-07-08 so the backlog holds runnable batch stories rather than
per-finding sediment. The original issues are closed with pointers here and
their bodies hold the full detail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] #1177 — routing selection is exercised at the lowest and highest complexity scores and at an out-of-range score. Current tests cover only mid-range values, so neither boundary nor the fallback for a score outside the range is reached.
- [ ] #1313 — the assertion on where a resolved model's registry entry came from names the expected source rather than accepting membership in a set of sources. As written it passes whether the model came from the builtin registry or from forge.yaml, so it cannot fail in either direction.
- [ ] #1314 — the registry source recorded in the complexity-routing audit is asserted for a model declared in forge.yaml, which no current test does.
- [ ] #1328 — the config check's branch for an unset per-story routing cost cap under adaptive routing is exercised.
- [ ] #1329 — the message reporting that no per-story routing cost cap is configured is asserted on, rather than only produced.
- [ ] Full gate passes.

## Example

The registry-source item. The current assertion accepts either possible source,
so a regression that silently switched a model from its forge.yaml declaration to
the builtin registry entry — or the reverse — leaves the test green. The
replacement asserts the single source the fixture actually configures, so either
direction of that regression fails.

Each remaining item has the same shape: a branch no current test reaches, or an
assertion present but too weak to fail when the behaviour it covers regresses.

## Currency

Findings were verified against `v0.10.0rc18` and re-checked on 2026-08-02 against
`v0.13.0rc16`. At that point the registry-source assertion was still valid though
its location had drifted, and both config-check items remained accurate. The two
routing items were not re-verified and should be confirmed before dispatch.

One finding from the original set — coverage of the canonical-identity emission
at the preflight seam — was dropped. The symbol it described no longer lives in
the module the finding named, and the seam as stated no longer exists. It is
recorded here as retired rather than silently removed; if the gap is real at the
identity layer it should be re-derived and filed fresh.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 instructs replacing the membership assertion at tests/test_config_load.py:835 with 'forge.yaml' as the single expected source. Executing that fixture shows config.dev_profile.registry_source is 'builtin' — the enabled list is ['anthropic/sonnet/cli', 'gpt-5.5'] and the dev role resolves to the builtin anthropic/sonnet/cli, not the forge.yaml-declared openai/gpt-5.5/cli. Asserting 'forge.yaml' fails. This is compounded by the plan's stated approach ('Keep production code untouched unless a new test exposes that the asserted behavior is missing'), which invites the dev agent to read the failure as a production defect and change model resolution — churn on correct code.
  Suggestion: Pick one and state it explicitly. (a) Keep the fixture and assert the true value: assert config.dev_profile.registry_source == 'builtin' — this satisfies #1313 as written, since the AC requires naming the expected source, not that the source be forge.yaml. (b) If asserting forge.yaml is the intent, first change the fixture so the custom model is the one dev resolves to (e.g. enabled: ['gpt-5.5'] only, or otherwise make openai/gpt-5.5/cli the strong-tier dev pick), then assert 'forge.yaml'. Either way, add a note that the pre-existing assertions at lines 831-834 already pin the forge.yaml source via model_registry_sources and must be kept.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 describes the out-of-range case as the '_normalize_complexity_score clamp/fallback path', but that function only clamps (max(1, min(10, ...))) — there is no distinct fallback branch for an out-of-range int. The None case is the fallback to the legacy PHASE_TIER band.
  Suggestion: Treat these as two separate cases: an out-of-range int (e.g. 99 or 0) that clamps to 10/1 and matches the boundary outcome, and complexity_score=None which falls back to the legacy band. Asserting both makes the clamp observable rather than coincidental.
- [P2] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 1's wording says 'clamp/fallback path', but src/theforge/assignment.py only exposes clamping in _normalize_complexity_score() for out-of-range numeric scores; there is no separate assignment-level fallback branch for numeric out-of-range input.
  Suggestion: Implement the out-of-range case by asserting that a score like 0 or 11 produces the same assignment as the clamped boundary score (1 or 10) through assign_models().

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
